creator: Alexander Terp
description:
The `bugfixes` board is a separate board from `main` and holds six open high-priority correctness bugs, each with a repro and a file:line fix pointer, all re-verified against v0.10.1 on 2026-06-14. They belong in this column on merit and were missed in the first pass of this sprint board.

| Bug | Tag |
|---|---|
| Caught errors re-propagate out of user functions | design |
| Nested loops clobber the outer loop's variables | design |
| Mutating a list while iterating skips elements | design |
| `error()` is not caught by `??` or `catch` | design |
| `??` / `catch` fails on negative literals | quick-win, grammar |
| No chained-call syntax - `make_adder(5)(3)` is a parse error | design |

Two are the same family as the `+=` bug above: nested-loop variable clobbering and caught-error re-propagation are both scope and control-flow resolution going wrong quietly.

Start with the `??`-on-negative-literals one - it's tagged quick-win and grammar, so it's contained.

Work them on the `bugfixes` board rather than duplicating the detail here; this card is the pointer so they don't get lost behind a board you aren't looking at this week.

Related: GitHub #140 proposes a property-based test harness for exactly this class, with metamorphic oracles (inlining a call must not change output; an unused local must change nothing). Its author notes each would have caught #137 alone. The `+=` bug is another it would have caught.

---

### Orientation

- Four of the six live in `core/`, the tree-walking interpreter. Two (`?? -1` and chained calls) are grammar gaps in the separate `amterp/tree-sitter-rad` repo, reached here through `rts/`.
- `rts/` owns the CST-to-AST conversion (`rts/converter.go`), the AST (`rts/rl/`), the checker (`rts/check/`) and the formatter (`rts/radfmt/`). A grammar change means editing the grammar upstream, bumping `github.com/amterp/tree-sitter-rad` in `go.mod` (currently v0.6.0), and handling the new node shape in `rts/converter.go`. `rts` must not import `core`.
- `radls/` inherits grammar and checker changes for free through `rts/`, but `rts/radfmt/` needs a print rule for any new syntax.
- Checkouts for the first-party deps live at `~/src/tree-sitter-rad` and `~/src/ra`. Iterate with a local `replace` directive in `go.mod` and remove it before committing - `./dev --release` refuses to release with one present.

### Where to start

Verified pointers, one per bug:

- **`??` / `catch` on a negative literal** (`a_sBPzQCcM`, tagged quick-win + grammar). Grammar-side, in `~/src/tree-sitter-rad`. The conversion side is `rts/converter.go:1094` `convertFallback` (`??`) and `rts/converter.go:1102` `convertCatchExpr` (`catch` as an expression); the AST nodes are `rl.Fallback` and `rl.CatchExpr` (`rts/rl/ast_types.go:334`). Formatter cases go under `rts/radfmt/snapshots/`. Start here as the card says.
- **Chained calls, `make_adder(5)(3)`** (`a_sBQ8LS6p`). Same grammar repo, much larger. `rl.Call.Func` is already a `Node`, so the AST can already carry a call as callee; the gap is the grammar's postfix chain, not the AST.
- **Nested loops clobber the outer loop variable** (`a_sBR0JLWj`). `core/interpreter.go:1103` `runForLoopList` and `core/interpreter.go:1165` `runForLoopMap` both write with `i.env.SetVar(vars[0], val)` (`:1132` and `:1188`) into the *current* env, so an inner loop reusing a name writes the same binding the outer loop is using. `core/interpreter.go:1224` `runWithChildEnv` is the existing child-scope helper to compare against.
- **Caught errors re-propagate out of user functions** (`a_sBRDpFgU`). `core/interpreter.go:844` `evalCatchingPanic`, `core/type_fn.go:81` (the user-fn call path, which is the only other `runWithChildEnv` caller), and the `RadPanic` construction (e.g. `core/shell.go:86`). The span-attribution sub-bug comes from the error value keeping the `SetSpan` from its original construction site.
- **`error()` not caught by `??` or `catch`** (`a_sBQgqO7u`). `core/interpreter.go:509`: the fallback condition is `if panicked || leftResult.Val.IsNull()`, with no `IsError()` arm. That is exactly the line the card's root-cause note describes.
- **Mutating a list while iterating skips elements** (`a_sBQtDAsa`). `core/interpreter.go:1128` ranges over `list.Values` live. `runForLoopMap` iterates `radMap.Keys()`, a snapshot, which is why the map repro no longer corrupts. Note the list loop already builds a `ShallowCopy()` at `core/interpreter.go:1121` for the `with` context - the same copy could back the iteration.

### How to verify

- `make build` produces `bin/radd`. Run each card's repro with `./bin/radd repro.rad`.
- End-to-end cases: `core/testing/snapshots/control_flow/` for the two loop bugs, `core/testing/snapshots/errors/` for the two catch bugs. Update with `go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=control_flow` and `-update=errors` (the `=` is required).
- Grammar changes additionally need `go test ./rts/ -run TestSTSnapshots -update=<path>` for `rts/test/st_snapshots/` and `go test ./rts/radfmt/ -run TestFmtSnapshots -update=<path>` for `rts/radfmt/snapshots/`.
- `make all` for the full loop, `./dev --validate` before wrapping up.
- Move each card as it lands: `kan edit <id> -b bugfixes -c done`.

### Done when

- All six cards sit in `done` on the `bugfixes` board, each with a snapshot case pinning the fixed behavior.
- No `replace` directive left in the committed `go.mod`.
- `make verify-generated` clean.

### Watch out for

- Two of the six are design calls before they are defect fixes: `error()` semantics and mutate-during-iteration. `docs/red/` holds the decision records - check for an existing RED before re-litigating, and write one if the answer is significant.
- Changing `error("x") ?? fallback` alters observable behavior for any script relying on the current asymmetry. That is a breaking change and carries the three-layer migration obligation from AGENTS.md: a migration diagnostic, a `core/error_docs/<code>.md` entry, and a section in `docs-web/docs/migrations/v0.X.md`. Commit prefix `fix!:`.
- The map half of `a_sBQtDAsa` no longer reproduces on current rad. Re-verify before touching the map path.
- The card says each bugfixes card carries a file:line fix pointer. They do not - they carry repros, re-verification dates, and root-cause or design notes. The pointers above are the missing half.
title: Clear the six todo-hi bugs on the bugfixes board
